definition: In manufacturing, an operational historian is a time-series database application that is developed for operational process data.
details: Historian software is often embedded or used in conjunction with standard DCS and PLC control systems to provide enhanced data capture, validation, compression, and aggregation capabilities. Historians have been deployed in almost every industry and contribute to functions such as supervisory control, performance monitoring, quality assurance, and, more recently, machine learning applications which can learn from vast quantities of historical data. These systems were originally developed to capture instrumentation and control data, which led many to use the term "tag" for a stream of process data, referring to the physical "tags" which had been placed on instrumentation for manually capturing data. Raw data may be accessed via OPC HDA, SQL, or REST API interfaces.

explainer.lead: An operational historian is a time-series database built for manufacturing process data. It matters because it captures and organizes the plant data that supervisory control, quality and machine learning later depend on.

tiers.eli5: It is a record book that constantly writes down readings from factory machines so people and computers can look back at them.
tiers.practitioner: Historians are embedded in or paired with DCS and PLC control systems to capture, validate, compress and aggregate data. A pitfall is trusting compressed data for fine-grained analysis, since compression and aggregation alter the stored signal.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a time-series database application for operational process data, often used with DCS and PLC systems, providing data capture, validation, compression and aggregation.

explainer.example: A plant historian logs sensor readings from PLCs, compresses them, and later serves the history to a quality-assurance dashboard.
